problem: 'the president' is never introduced (a stranger asks: president of what?), and the hackers carry two stacked descriptions ('we told you about on Sunday' then 'who leaked customers' personal data'), so the sentence is hard to follow on one hearing. The fix reads Seoul as South Korea's president; check that against the source.
fix: South Korea's president sees signs A I helped the hackers who leaked bank customers' personal data. We told you about that hack on Sunday.

problem: It never says why this matters to ordinary people, only to companies. 'A top free Chinese one' leaves 'one' far from the 'A I' it stands for, and 'as we said yesterday it would' breaks into the middle of the sentence. The fix clears the wording but cannot add a reason for ordinary people without new facts; the writer should add one from the source.
fix: Start-up Reflection has unveiled Beam, a new American A I, as we said yesterday it would. It claims firms can use Beam in place of a top free Chinese A I.
